An operating system for AI agents

The autonomous control plane for your agents.

See and steer every Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor session.
Always-on agents check in on their own, and you step in only when one needs you.

Download · Docs · Marketplace · Changelog · Blog

The bottleneck stopped being the model. It became managing the sessions. Run Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor in parallel and you end up with five terminals, a prompt typed into the wrong one, and no clear view of which agent is waiting on you. Keeping them working means gluing loops, cron, webhooks, and approvals together by hand. CompozyOS replaces the pile, not one tool in it. It runs the agent CLIs you already have as sessions that outlive the terminal, keeps every one of them visible, and calls you only when a decision is yours. Loops, schedules, permissions, and approvals come built in, so there is no stack to assemble around the agent. ## Install ```bash curl -fsSL https://compozy.com/install.sh | sh ``` The verified installer pins the latest release and checks its Sigstore provenance before it installs the binary on macOS or Linux. Prefer the desktop app? [Download it for macOS or Linux](https://compozy.com/download).
Homebrew, npm, Go, or from source ```bash # Homebrew brew install compozy/compozy/compozy # npm npm install -g @compozy/cli # Go, with the tag shown on https://github.com/compozy/compozy/releases/latest go install github.com/compozy/compozy@ # From source git clone https://github.com/compozy/compozy.git cd compozy go build -o ./bin/compozy . ``` The CLI runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows. The [installation guide](https://compozy.com/docs/getting-started/installation) covers installer flags, Linux packages, verification, and managed updates.
Then start one session, from the repository you want agents to work on: ```bash compozy install # pick a provider (the verified installer opens this for you) compozy daemon start # start the local daemon compozy session new --agent general --name first-run ``` The [Quick Start](https://compozy.com/docs/getting-started/quick-start) continues through the first prompt, live attachment, inspection, and cleanup. Today's experience is technical: a terminal, a local daemon, and a `config.toml`. ## Every session, sorted by who owns the next step

Every session lands in Needs you, Working, Waiting, In review, or Done. Needs you is the only loud colour on the screen, so you know where to look. - **Worktrees** give parallel agents their own checkout of the same repository. - **The branch, the pull request, and its checks** sit on the session. - **Handoff** continues a session with another agent CLI when one runs out. - **Approvals** hold a tool call until a person allows it, and waiting work rises to Needs you. ## Agents that check in on their own

An always-on agent has a name, a face, and one main session per project. It reviews its work on a schedule, stays quiet when there is nothing to say, and calls you when something needs a decision. - **Check-ins.** On a schedule, the agent reviews its project in a hidden, read-only session. A quiet check costs no model call. - **Sources.** Point it at what it should watch: new GitHub issues from an extension, or a script you approve. - **Reports.** Reports land in its main session. Come back after a day away and one card sums up what happened. - **Proposals.** Pick a proposed action, or let the agent do it without asking, up to a daily limit you set. Agents keep notes on purpose. Nothing is extracted behind your back. Check-ins need Claude, Codex, or OpenCode. Start with [Watch new GitHub issues](https://compozy.com/docs/guides/watch-new-github-issues). ## Agents hand work to each other, not to you

A session delegates to subagents and watches their progress live. An agent can end its turn and wake when a pull request's checks finish, another session settles, or a command exits, so nobody has to sit in the terminal waiting for it. ## Loops stop when the goal is verified

A Loop is a named contract: a goal, a way to verify it, and a stop. The daemon runs it unattended and always ends it honestly. - Bounded by design: every Loop carries an iteration cap. - A human gate parks the run until someone approves, requests changes, or rejects. - Seven named endings: done, no-op, blocked, failed, exhausted, stalled, canceled. - The same run from the web, the CLI, and HTTP. No Loops ship by default. Write one, fork one, or install an extension that ships one. Read the [Loops guide](https://compozy.com/docs/loops). ## Put agent work on a schedule or an event

Schedules, runtime triggers, and signed webhooks live in one place. Every run is recorded, and finished runs leave your session list on their own. A briefing can be waiting for you every weekday at 08:30, with nobody watching it start. ## Runs the agents you already use CompozyOS starts the agent CLIs you already have as durable sessions you can see, steer, and hand off. It is not another agent competing with them. Fifteen integrations are built in: | Agent CLIs | Model providers and gateways | | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | | Claude Code · Codex · Cursor Agent · Gemini CLI · Google Antigravity · GitHub Copilot CLI · OpenCode · Pi · Kimi CLI · Qwen Code | OpenRouter · Vercel AI Gateway · xAI · z.ai · Moonshot / Kimi | Your subscriptions and API keys stay yours. CompozyOS resells no model access. See [supported agents](https://compozy.com/docs/agents/providers) for authentication and provider setup. ## Comes with what you would otherwise build | Built in | What you get | | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | **Sessions** | Agent work that outlives the terminal. Fork a session, continue it with another agent, rewind to a checkpoint, or steer it mid-turn. | | **Files** | Browse and search the project, and review a session's diff against its base. | | **Terminal** | Runtime-owned shells you can open, watch, and hand to an agent. | | **Desktops** | Persistent desktops with browser-style tabs and side-by-side splits, a command palette, and a global hotkey. | | **Workspaces** | See all projects at once, work without a project, and give parallel agents their own worktree. | | **Tasks** | Durable work a session claims, heartbeats, and closes with evidence. | | **Profiles** | Separate work on one install. An operating system for AI agents

The autonomous control plane for your agents.

See and steer every Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor session.
Always-on agents check in on their own, and you step in only when one needs you.

Download · Docs · Marketplace · Changelog · Blog

The bottleneck stopped being the model. It became managing the sessions. Run Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor in parallel and you end up with five terminals, a prompt typed into the wrong one, and no clear view of which agent is waiting on you. Keeping them working means gluing loops, cron, webhooks, and approvals together by hand.

CompozyOS replaces the pile, not one tool in it. It runs the agent CLIs you already have as sessions that outlive the terminal, keeps every one of them visible, and calls you only when a decision is yours. Loops, schedules, permissions, and approvals come built in, so there is no stack to assemble around the agent.

Install

curl -fsSL https://compozy.com/install.sh | sh

The verified installer pins the latest release and checks its Sigstore provenance before it installs the binary on macOS or Linux. Prefer the desktop app? Download it for macOS or Linux.

Homebrew, npm, Go, or from source 
# Homebrew
brew install compozy/compozy/compozy

# npm
npm install -g @compozy/cli

# Go, with the tag shown on https://github.com/compozy/compozy/releases/latest
go install github.com/compozy/compozy@<release-tag>

# From source
git clone https://github.com/compozy/compozy.git
cd compozy
go build -o ./bin/compozy .

The CLI runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows. The installation guide covers installer flags, Linux packages, verification, and managed updates.

Then start one session, from the repository you want agents to work on:

compozy install        # pick a provider (the verified installer opens this for you)
compozy daemon start   # start the local daemon
compozy session new --agent general --name first-run

The Quick Start continues through the first prompt, live attachment, inspection, and cleanup. Today's experience is technical: a terminal, a local daemon, and a config.toml.

Every session, sorted by who owns the next step

Every session lands in Needs you, Working, Waiting, In review, or Done. Needs you is the only loud colour on the screen, so you know where to look.

  • Worktrees give parallel agents their own checkout of the same repository.
  • The branch, the pull request, and its checks sit on the session.
  • Handoff continues a session with another agent CLI when one runs out.
  • Approvals hold a tool call until a person allows it, and waiting work rises to Needs you.

Agents that check in on their own

An always-on agent has a name, a face, and one main session per project. It reviews its work on a schedule, stays quiet when there is nothing to say, and calls you when something needs a decision.

  • Check-ins. On a schedule, the agent reviews its project in a hidden, read-only session. A quiet check costs no model call.
  • Sources. Point it at what it should watch: new GitHub issues from an extension, or a script you approve.
  • Reports. Reports land in its main session. Come back after a day away and one card sums up what happened.
  • Proposals. Pick a proposed action, or let the agent do it without asking, up to a daily limit you set.

Agents keep notes on purpose. Nothing is extracted behind your back. Check-ins need Claude, Codex, or OpenCode. Start with Watch new GitHub issues.

Agents hand work to each other, not to you

A session delegates to subagents and watches their progress live. An agent can end its turn and wake when a pull request's checks finish, another session settles, or a command exits, so nobody has to sit in the terminal waiting for it.

Loops stop when the goal is verified

A Loop is a named contract: a goal, a way to verify it, and a stop. The daemon runs it unattended and always ends it honestly.

  • Bounded by design: every Loop carries an iteration cap.
  • A human gate parks the run until someone approves, requests changes, or rejects.
  • Seven named endings: done, no-op, blocked, failed, exhausted, stalled, canceled.
  • The same run from the web, the CLI, and HTTP.

No Loops ship by default. Write one, fork one, or install an extension that ships one. Read the Loops guide.

Put agent work on a schedule or an event

Schedules, runtime triggers, and signed webhooks live in one place. Every run is recorded, and finished runs leave your session list on their own. A briefing can be waiting for you every weekday at 08:30, with nobody watching it start.

Runs the agents you already use

CompozyOS starts the agent CLIs you already have as durable sessions you can see, steer, and hand off. It is not another agent competing with them. Fifteen integrations are built in:

Agent CLIs Model providers and gateways
Claude Code · Codex · Cursor Agent · Gemini CLI · Google Antigravity · GitHub Copilot CLI · OpenCode · Pi · Kimi CLI · Qwen Code OpenRouter · Vercel AI Gateway · xAI · z.ai · Moonshot / Kimi

Your subscriptions and API keys stay yours. CompozyOS resells no model access. See supported agents for authentication and provider setup.

Comes with what you would otherwise build

Built in What you get
Sessions Agent work that outlives the terminal. Fork a session, continue it with another agent, rewind to a checkpoint, or steer it mid-turn.
Files Browse and search the project, and review a session's diff against its base.
Terminal Runtime-owned shells you can open, watch, and hand to an agent.
Desktops Persistent desktops with browser-style tabs and side-by-side splits, a command palette, and a global hotkey.
Workspaces See all projects at once, work without a project, and give parallel agents their own worktree.
Tasks Durable work a session claims, heartbeats, and closes with evidence.
Profiles Separate work on one install. Profiles organize work; they are not a security boundary.
Gateway The daemon starts reachable only on this machine. Remote access is off until you turn it on.

And the smaller things: park a session for Later with a reason and a date, folders and bulk actions, a vault that keeps secrets out of config files, hooks on daemon events, skills from any source, MCP sign-in, a curated model catalog, session health, and one-click updates.

What people run on it

  • Triage new issues as they land. An always-on agent watches new GitHub issues. It proposes what to do; you pick.
  • Deliver a spec while you are away. A conductor splits the work into slices. Each slice runs in its own worktree.
  • Review a change until the round is clean. A reviewer finds, an implementer fixes. Findings land in a file you can open.
  • Leave a briefing waiting every weekday. A schedule starts an agent with nobody watching. Every run is recorded, with retry on failure.
  • Keep release checks as claimed work. Each concern is a task an agent claims. Runs close with evidence.
  • Wait for a person before a sensitive action. A tool call can require approval before it runs.

The use cases walk through each one.

Built to be built on

Extensions, plugins, and MCP servers share one Marketplace, by category, with one-step Add. An extension brings skills, agents, tools, hooks, and check-in sources into the same registries your agents already use.

Write one in Go or TypeScript, with React for views:

compozy extension init hello --template tool-provider-go
compozy extension dev hello
compozy tool invoke ext__hello__search --workspace . --input '{"query":"compozy"}'
  • Extensions. @compozy/extension-sdk (npm) and github.com/compozy/compozy/sdk/go are published and version-matched to the daemon. Start with Build your first extension.
  • Apps. @compozy/client (TypeScript) and github.com/compozy/compozy/sdk/go/client (Go) connect an external app to your running daemon, with typed operations and agent streams. These surfaces are experimental; pin the version that matches your daemon. See Build an app.
  • Agents. The official CompozyOS skill teaches an agent to operate the runtime through the same contracts people use.

How it works

flowchart LR
  people(["People"]) --> surfaces
  agents(["Agents"]) --> surfaces
  surfaces["Desktop and web · CLI · HTTP/SSE · UDS · MCP · native tools"] --> daemon
  daemon["compozy daemon<br/>sessions · tasks · Loops · automations · approvals"]
  daemon --> clis["Agent CLIs over ACP<br/>Claude Code · Codex · Cursor · …"]
  daemon --> state[("SQLite state<br/>on your machine")]
  daemon --> ext["Extensions · hooks · skills"]
Loading

One Go binary runs a local daemon that owns every session, task, Loop run, and approval, and talks to agent CLIs over ACP (Agent Client Protocol). The desktop app, the web UI, the CLI, HTTP/SSE, the Unix socket, MCP, and native tools all read and change that same state, so people and agents manage the same work and nothing has to be glued together. State stays in SQLite on your machine unless a provider or extension you configure owns an external boundary.

compozy status
compozy session list -o json
compozy doctor -o json

Documentation

Start Go deeper Reference
Installation Sessions CLI
Quick Start Loops HTTP API
Supported agents Automation SDKs
Guides Extensions Configuration
Use cases Gateway Changelog

Note

Coming from v0.2? That product has reached end of life and receives no further releases. Read the migration guide before replacing an existing v0.2 installation.

Development

CompozyOS is a Go and Bun monorepo. Start the daemon with automatic Go rebuilds and the web UI with Vite HMR:

make dev

To explore the product with realistic data, seed the Northstar Pay demo. It builds the daemon and web bundle and serves the demo at http://localhost:2124 from ~/.compozy-demo, leaving your main instance unchanged:

make demo-seed            # web UI
make demo-seed-desktop    # the same demo in the Electron desktop shell

# Optional isolated home and port:
make demo-seed DEMO_HOME="$HOME/.compozy-demo-other" DEMO_PORT=2125

The demo daemon keeps running in the background. Stop it before reseeding:

COMPOZY_HOME="$HOME/.compozy-demo" ./bin/compozy daemon stop

Read AGENTS.md and the surface-specific instructions before editing. Run focused tests and lint for what you changed; CI owns the full gate, and a pull request is done when every required check passes on its current head.

Contributing

Contributions are welcome. Open an issue or a pull request, and keep public behavior manageable by agents through the CLI, HTTP, and UDS surfaces. Security reports belong in the repository's private security channel, not a public issue.

License

CompozyOS is distributed under the MIT License.

### Features

- Optional OpenTelemetry trace and metric export (#1552)
- Make the update button prominent with an animated brand border (#1623)



### Performance Improvements

- Read a session's instance binding by key instead of a catalog list (#1632)



### Testing

- Wait for obsolete attention wake settlement

### Release Notes

#### Features

##### Export daemon traces and metrics with OpenTelemetry
CompozyOS can now export daemon traces and metrics to an OpenTelemetry collector over OTLP HTTP or gRPC. Export is off by default. aiSummary.oneLiner: Local-first operating system connecting disparate AI agent CLIs into a unified collaborative team.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: CompozyOS provides a durable, local runtime environment that effectively connects multiple isolated AI agent CLIs into a highly collaborative project team. It utilizes a robust local daemon to actively manage shared project memory, tasks, permissions, and tool execution across agents like Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor. Developers interact with the agents through a sophisticated web shell and CLI, steering the automated jobs and complex loops in real-time. The agents interface dynamically with the system state using structured HTTP, UDS, and native tool surfaces, providing a cohesive workspace that survives terminal closures.
keyFeatures: Agent Orchestration: Seamlessly connects disparate agent CLIs to split tasks, hand off work, and run automated execution loops.
Shared Project Memory: Maintains a single, durable source of context and state that all connected agents can continuously access.
Local Daemon Architecture: Runs entirely locally to securely handle session management, complex permissions, and tool coordination.
Browser-Based Steering: Provides a rich web shell interface for human supervisors to effectively monitor and steer the automated agents.
Standardized Interfaces: Exposes deep system state to agents via structured HTTP, UDS, MCP, and native integrated tools.
Extension Ecosystem: Features a flexible extension architecture allowing developers to build and plug in new tool surfaces effortlessly.

useCases.title: Building Collaborative AI Teams
useCases.description: Plugging in specialized agents for frontend and backend development to work together seamlessly on a single full-stack feature.

useCases.title: Automating Background Workflows
useCases.description: Setting up autonomous agent loops to continuously monitor, review, and fix codebase quality issues running in the background.

useCases.title: Managing Multi-Agent State
useCases.description: Providing a durable, centralized memory store for agents that typically lose valuable context after closing their terminal sessions.

useCases.title: Browser-Supervised Automation
useCases.description: Using the web shell to visually track complex task hand-offs and quickly intervene when agents require specific human feedback.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Software engineers and AI researchers looking to orchestrate multiple independent agent CLIs into a highly cohesive, locally managed development team. It is essential for those actively adopting sophisticated multi-agent pipelines.
